title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Process, Runbooks, Rotations, Game Days, Status & Comms
author: Ethan Brooks
summary: Canonical playbook for on-call and incident response at Redwood Inference: incident lifecycle, runbook templates, severity taxonomy, rotation rules, game-day guidance, postmortem process, and customer/status communications templates.
body:
Overview
This playbook documents the standard process for detecting, triaging, responding to, and learning from incidents that affect Redwood Inference production services. It is intended for on-call engineers, incident commanders (ICs), SREs, product owners, and support staff. Use this as the single source of truth for operational behavior, escalation, and external communications.

Incident lifecycle (summary)
1) Detection & Alerting: automated alerts (Prometheus/Alertmanager, Datadog, Sentry) or manual reports (support, customers).
2) Triage: assign an incident ID, determine scope & impact, classify severity.
3) Response: assign roles (IC, primary/secondary, comms lead), run targeted runbooks, mitigate customer impact.
4) Mitigation & Recovery: restore service, enable degradations or fallbacks, verify recovery metrics.
5) Postmortem & RCA: create an incident report within 72 hours, run a blameless postmortem, and track action items.

Detection & alerting (detailed)
- Alert sources: Prometheus (service-level latency/5xx), Datadog (synthetics, host metrics), Sentry (exceptions), PagerDuty (escalations), Customer reports (Zendesk).
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - API 95th percentile latency > 800ms for > 3m -> P1 alert.
  - Error rate (5xx) > 1% of requests over 5m -> P1.
  - GPU node OOM / host down -> P0 / P1 depending on cluster impact.
- Alert enrichment: alerts must include service, region, incident-id (if known), top error message, and relevant runbook link.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1) Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty and create an incident in the standard tracker (confluence incident page template / incident tracker).
2) Determine impact: user-visible outage, degraded latency, or background job failures.
3) Assign severity (see taxonomy below).
4) Identify primary owner and IC. Post an initial summary in #incidents and tag IC and on-call.
5) Run the appropriate service runbook (link to runbook matrix below).

Severity taxonomy & business impact guidelines
- SEV0 (Critical): Full production outage with customer-visible data loss or inability for all customers to make progress. Target SLOs: immediate paging, <15 min response.
- SEV1 (High): Significant degradation for many customers (major API errors, high latency). Target: <30m response and mitigation plan.
- SEV2 (Medium): Partial degradation, single-region impact, or reduced throughput. Target: investigate within 4 hours.
- SEV3 (Low): Non-urgent operational issues or feature regressions with minimal customer impact. Track as ticket.

Roles & responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): owns the incident lifecycle, decisions, and timeline. Decides when to escalate or declare operational recovery.
- Primary On-Call (service owner): executes runbooks, provides technical context, triages root cause.
- Secondary / Backup: picks up if primary unavailable, assists with mitigation and code rollbacks.
- Communications Lead: drafts and publishes status page updates and customer emails.
- SWAT / Engineering Support: cross-team specialists (network, infra, runtime, model-serving) called in for complex incidents.
- Postmortem Author: usually the IC or primary owner; responsible for writing the RCA and recording action items.

Escalation matrix (reference table)
Role | Primary contact | Slack channel | Pager duty escalation
--- | --- | --- | ---
Primary on-call | Service rotation owner list | #service-oncall | Level-0
Secondary | Team on-call | #team-oncall | Level-1
IC (if escalated) | Senior SRE / Engineering Manager | #incidents | Level-2
Executive escalation | VP Eng / Head of Product | #exec-incident | Direct call

Runbook templates & examples
- Runbook purpose: provide a concise, actionable set of steps to (a) identify the immediate cause, (b) apply a targeted mitigation, (c) validate recovery, and (d) perform a safe rollback or configuration change if required.
- Every runbook should include: pre-reqs, ownership, runbook steps (numbered), verification steps, rollback instructions, and post-incident notes.

Example: API Gateway High-Error-Rate runbook (summary)
Prerequisites: cluster-admin rights, kubectl configured, access to logging (Loki/Datadog) and tracing (Tempo).
Steps:
1) Gather quick signals: 5xx spike graphs, recent deploys, error sample from Sentry.
2) Check deployment status: kubectl get pods -n api | grep CrashLoopBackOff.
3) Check Nginx/Envoy logs for 502/504 patterns: kubectl logs -l app=ingress -n infra --tail=200.
4) If rollout coincides, roll back to previous revision: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-v2 -n api.
5) If database connection errors present, verify DB connection pool saturation and fail open/close accordingly.
Verification: success is 5xx rate returning to baseline (<= 0.1%) for 10 minutes.
Post-incident: capture commands run and paste into incident page.

Example: GPU Fleet Node Loss runbook (summary)
Prerequisites: access to cluster nodes and GPU monitoring, runbook link to GPU-fleet playbook.
Steps:
1) Identify affected nodes and VMs: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters ... or gcloud compute instances list --filter=...
2) Drain impacted nodes: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
3) Replace node or trigger autoscaler group recreate.
4) Monitor queued jobs and fallback to a smaller model variant if throughput is impacted.
Verification: scheduled jobs resume, % unscheduled eviction < 0.5% for 30m.

Rotation rules & scheduling
- Standard rotation: 1-week primary on-call shifts for product teams, with 24x7 paging.
- On-call expectations: respond to pages within 15 minutes during business hours and 30 minutes overnight for SEV1/SEV0.
- Handoffs: every Sunday at 09:00 PT the outgoing on-call must run the handoff checklist and post a Handoff Note in #oncall-handoffs.
- Vacation & swap: use the on-call roster tool (pagerduty roster / internal rota) to request swaps at least 72 hours in advance.
- Escalation: if primary does not acknowledge within escalation timeout, page secondary then IC, and finally execs.

Game days (purpose & runbook)
Purpose: validate runbooks, cross-team coordination, and resilience of critical flows.
Frequency: quarterly for high-risk services (API, serving-runtime, routing), bi-annually for others.
Game day format:
- Preparation (1 week): define scope, failure injection plan, observers, and metrics to capture.
- Execution day: run the exercise (simulated deploy failure, region outage, or GPU fleet loss).
- Debrief (within 48h): write observations, update runbooks, and create action items.
Outcomes tracked in the Game Days tracker and assigned as JIRA tickets.

Postmortem & RCA process
- Trigger: SEV0/SEV1 incidents or any incident with customer impact or data loss.
- Timeline:
  - Initial incident page within 2 hours summarizing impact and mitigation steps.
  - Draft postmortem within 72 hours with timeline, root cause hypothesis, evidence, and action items.
  - Postmortem review meeting within 7 business days.
  - Action items assigned with clear owners and due dates; tracked until closed.
- Postmortem template fields (required):
  - Title, incident_id, date/time window, severity, services affected, incident lead (IC), summary, timeline of events, root cause, contributing factors, mitigations taken, detection & alerting gaps, corrective action items, owners, due dates, and lessons learned.
- Blameless language guidance: avoid naming individuals as root cause; focus on process, automation, and system gaps.

Metrics & SLOs to track post-incident
- Time to acknowledge (target P1 < 15m).
- Time to mitigation (target P1 < 60m).
- Time to full recovery (target varies by service; record the target per-service SLO).
- Number of regressions from the same root cause (goal: 0 in 90 days).

Status page & customer communication templates
- Use the status.redwood.ai status page for public incidents and email/Salesforce for high-impact customers. Communications must be coordinated by the Communications Lead.

Initial public status update (template):
Title: [Incident {{incident_id}}] Degraded service for Redwood API — investigating
Body:
We are currently investigating reports of degraded API performance impacting some customers in {{region}}. Engineers are actively investigating. Scope: {{brief scope}}.
Impact: {{brief impact}}.
Next update: within 30 minutes or sooner.

Customer notification (high-impact) — initial email template:
Subject: Redwood Incident {{incident_id}} — Service degradation impacting API
Body:
Hello {{customer_name}},
We are investigating an issue affecting Redwood API in {{region}} that may impact request latency and embeddings throughput. Our on-call team is actively working to isolate and mitigate the issue. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.
If you require assistance or mitigation steps, reply to this email and we will prioritize the request.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Ops

Status update (follow-up) template:
Title: [Incident {{incident_id}}] Update — mitigation in progress
Body:
Summary of changes since last update: {{actions taken}}
Current impact: {{current impact}}
Next steps: {{next steps and ETA}}

Resolution & RCA summary (public) template:
Title: [Incident {{incident_id}}] Resolved — summary and next steps
Body:
Impact: {{final impact summary}}
Root cause: {{concise root cause}}
Mitigation: {{what restored service}}
Actions: {{short list of actions to prevent recurrence}}
Link to full postmortem: {{confluence link}}

Comms runbook (internal checklist)
1) Draft initial status and post to status page and #incidents.
2) Notify affected account managers for high-impact customers.
3) Prepare customer email draft and route to legal/product for review if data exposure suspected.
4) Schedule postmortem and assign author.

Post-incident follow-up & tracking
- Action items: create actionable JIRA tickets with owners, priority, and due dates.
- Runbook updates: update runbooks within 7 days if steps were unclear or missing.
- Retro & distribution: share postmortem summary with relevant teams and at the fortnightly ops review.

Appendices
A. Incident page checklist (minimum content)
- Title and incident id
- Severity
- Start time and detection source
- Summary of impact
- Services affected and ownership
- Mitigations applied and timeline
- Logs/queries/commands used
- Postmortem link when available

B. Useful commands & quick queries
- kubectl get pods -A -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl logs -l app=<service> -n <ns> --tail=200
- aws autoscaling describe-auto-scaling-instances --region <region>
- datadog monitor search 'service:<service>'

C. Where to find runbooks
All team runbooks live under Confluence: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks and must include owner metadata and last-tested date.

Document ownership & maintenance
This playbook is owned by the Engineering (SRE) organization. The on-call lead must review this document quarterly and after every SEV0/SEV1 incident.

If you are reading this during an incident: follow the triage checklist above, acknowledge your page, and post an initial incident note in #incidents immediately.
